A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe LCDrive. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original PhysicalAI-AV driving evaluations, reasoning-action analyses, and reasoning-budget ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds wall-clock inference measurements and training-compute results.

M1.justification: The interleaved action/world-model reasoning, architecture, cold-start losses, and ADE-reward GRPO procedure remain unchanged. Revised RL terminology and the newly disclosed AR1 initialization do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PhysicalAI-AV driving coverage and 15 scenario categories. The added runtime measurements introduce no new dataset, driving task, or environmental test scenario.

E2.justification: The efficiency comparison expands from the text-versus-latent cost comparison in v1 Appendix C.2 to a runtime comparison including Text CoT, LCDrive, LCDrive-Light, and No CoT in v2 Table 3. Comparator membership in the main driving tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a runtime protocol using an RTX A5000, batch size 1, identical decoding settings, and phase latency, throughput, and memory measurements. The driving splits, metrics, and six-trajectory sampling remain unchanged. The reported 42-token timing configuration is not reconciled with the retained default of approximately 120 tokens.

E4.justification: v2 adds inference-phase profiling and a lighter-budget timing comparison, examining where latency savings arise. The existing reasoning-action analysis and depth/branch ablations remain unchanged, moving from Appendices B/C to C/D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing token-length summary statistics remain unchanged, and the new runtime results add no repeated-measurement counts or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, the reasoning-action table, and Figure 5 retain their results. New Tables 3–4 report reasoning latencies of 2446.6 ms for Text CoT, 1388.1 ms for LCDrive, and 754.8 ms for LCDrive-Light, plus 641 GPU-hours of training. Section 4.2 also corrects the reported scenario ranking from universal LCDrive superiority to mixed outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, losses, and reasoning-analysis definitions are retained. Changing reward notation from R to r and explaining existing policy/transition symbols adds no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion replace claims of closed-loop or interactive RL with trajectory-reward RL post-training. The abstract also drops its explicit Text CoT comparison, although that comparison remains in the introduction and conclusion. The central latent-reasoning contribution is retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 acknowledges Text CoT advantages on Cut-In and Lead Vehicle Following and introduces a proactive-versus-reactive explanation. It also newly claims predicted LWM preserves most oracle gains, which Table 1's ADE values do not support. The supervision, interpretability, and fixed-reasoning-length limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses AR1 checkpoint initialization, A100 hardware, and stage-specific training time and compute. Appendix B reports policy-optimization batch size 96 without reconciling the retained 32 sampled completions per update in Section 4.1. The explicit cosmos-rl repository footnote is removed, while the framework remains named.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to OmniDrive, FutureSightDrive, and retrieval-based interleaved visual CoT. A new related-work passage distinguishes their scope and explains the choice of AR1 as the closest available open-source text-CoT comparator; these cited additions are not experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: v2 fixes wording and typos, clarifies existing symbols and the inference-time meaning of E2E, and condenses the qualitative discussion and conclusion. It inserts a runtime/compute appendix and renumbers subsequent appendices, while retaining most of the narrative and technical exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime and compute Tables 3–4, relocates and renumbers the original reasoning-action table as Table 5, and moves Figure 5 within the appendix layout. Existing figures and main table structures are retained; the document undergoes limited reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Partially correcting the false all-scenario superiority statement and replacing closed-loop RL claims improve fidelity to the retained evidence. Checkpoint and compute disclosures also improve transparency. These gains are limited by remaining scenario/oracle overclaims, inconsistent batch-size reporting, and the unexplained 42-token timing configuration versus the approximately 120-token default; the new speedup therefore does not clearly validate the main accuracy configuration.
